sections.heading: C — Sharing the road and work zones
sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the road and work zones

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Work zones contain construction, maintenance or utility operations and use orange channelizers or temporary traffic controls. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
Work-zone warnings, vehicles or message boards may be positioned at least 200 feet before the work area. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
From the first work-zone warning, attend closely to the roadway, vehicles, equipment and people. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Do not pass a moving road-work operation unless directed to do so. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
An active work zone has workers on or near the road and may have narrow lanes, rough pavement or abrupt lane shifts. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
Yield to workers and construction vehicles in work zones. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
Use actual headlights in work zones rather than daytime running lights alone. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A01
Certain active-work-zone fines, including speeding penalties, are doubled and some violations can suspend the license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A01
Consider another route to avoid work-zone delays. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A01
Do not use cruise control in a work zone. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A01
Double the normal following gap in work zones. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A01
Prepare to change lanes when the first message announces the lane closure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A01
Stay in the lane and do not cross a solid white work-zone line. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A01
Continue cautiously at a safe speed rather than stopping or slowing just to watch the work. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A01
Do not stop within a work zone to ask workers for directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A01
Follow flagger directions, which take precedence over conventional traffic-control devices. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A01
Flaggers may report unsafe driving, speeding and aggression to police using a Police Arrest Form. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
Look left, right and left again approaching tracks even if installed signals are not flashing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A02
After a train clears multiple tracks, wait for a clear view along both tracks before crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A02
Even at a single track, check for another train before crossing after the first passes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A02
Do not pass another vehicle while approaching or entering a rail crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A02
Enter tracks only when there is room to clear them completely, waiting if traffic ahead is backed up. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A02
If trapped on tracks with a train approaching, leave the vehicle quickly and move as far from the track as possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A02
Yield to pedestrians at intersections and crosswalks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A02
Before a right turn on red, stop and scan all directions, allowing pedestrians time to clear the crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A02
Slow down and take extra care near children. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A02
Allow older pedestrians and people with disabilities extra time to cross. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A02
Check for pedestrians before reversing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A02
Slow and prepare to stop for a blind pedestrian using a cane, guide dog or another person's guidance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F30 | anchor: A02
Before passing a stopped vehicle, slow and verify no pedestrian is crossing ahead of it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F31 | anchor: A02
Do not wave a pedestrian into traffic, especially at unmarked or mid-block crossings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-F32 | anchor: A03
On level roads, passing a truck takes three to five seconds longer than passing a passenger vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F33 | anchor: A03
A truck may slow uphill or gain momentum downhill, changing the passing situation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F34 | anchor: A03
Leave room ahead in the passing lane, pass without lingering beside the truck and hold the wheel with both hands against turbulence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F35 | anchor: A03
Return after passing a truck only when its front or headlights can be seen in the rearview mirror, then maintain speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F36 | anchor: A03
At highway speed, safely passing a truck can take as long as 30 seconds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F37 | anchor: A03
Slow to a safe speed when approaching or passing a cyclist. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F38 | anchor: A03
Avoid abrupt slowing or stopping immediately after passing a bicycle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F39 | anchor: A03
Do not sound the horn close to a cyclist unless needed to avert a crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F40 | anchor: A03
Give a motorcycle or moped the use of a complete lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F41 | anchor: A03
Wait for a motorcycle or moped to actually begin turning rather than relying on its flashing indicator. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F42 | anchor: A03
Be ready for a motorcycle or moped to change speed or lane suddenly to avoid a road hazard. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F43 | anchor: A03
Follow motorcycles or mopeds by at least four seconds and increase the gap in bad weather or road conditions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-F44 | anchor: A04
When a truck passes, stay toward the far side of your lane, ease speed slightly if helpful and keep it steady without accelerating. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-F45 | anchor: A04
If a truck begins merging while you occupy its blind spot, stay calm, judge position and choose slowing or accelerating to avoid collision, considering a side escape. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-F46 | anchor: A04
When meeting an oncoming truck, keep as far to the side as possible and preserve a forward cushion. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-F47 | anchor: A04
Follow far enough back that the truck driver can see the vehicle in the truck's side mirrors. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-F48 | anchor: A04
If a truck's or bus's side mirrors cannot be seen, its driver cannot see the following vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-F49 | anchor: A04
Leave extra stopping room behind a truck uphill because it may roll backward. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-F50 | anchor: A04
Dim headlights when following a truck or another vehicle at night. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-F51 | anchor: A04
Keep at least four seconds behind a truck, timing its passage of a fixed object until the front bumper reaches that point. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-F52 | anchor: A04
Do not pass a turning truck until the turn is complete; it may need adjoining space to clear the corner. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-F53 | anchor: A04
Do not squeeze between a right-turning truck and the curb; its driver may be unable to see the vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0061]

Misconceptions: daytime running lights do not replace work-zone headlights; a truck's side mirrors indicate whether its driver can see a following vehicle; school-bus stopping has a physical-divider exception.
Mnemonics: watch the worker, leave the large vehicle space and protect vulnerable road users.
Glossary: a No-Zone is a large vehicle's blind area; a pilot vehicle warns of an oversized load; an escape ramp serves runaway heavy vehicles.
Dynamic facts: no officeholder, local answer or time-varying value is asserted; handbook edition currency is tracked as source debt in the authority part.
